title: RENTING A CAR
conversation: Sam: Hello. How can I help you? Peter: I'd like to rent a car for the weekend. Sam: What size do you have in mind? Peter: I'd like your cheapest car, so I guess that would be a compact. Sam: We're running a special right now. You can rent a mid-size car for the same price as a compact. It's $55 a day inclusive of tax, plus insurance. It's such a great deal! Peter: Okay, I'll take it. Sam: All right. Let me just print out the agreement. . . Here you go, read over that, please. Peter: I can't make heads or tails of this information. Do I really need insurance? I already have a good auto insurance plan. Sam: Then you're probably all set. I do recommend the collision damage waiver.* It's only $10 a day. That way, if you bang up the car, you won't owe us anything. Peter: I'm sure I won't have an accident, but I'll take it just in case. Sam: Very good. If you don't return the car with a full tank of gas, we charge $9 a gallon to refill it. Peter: Nine bucks a gallon? That's so expensive. It's highway robbery! Sam: Be sure to return the car by 5 p.m. on Sunday. Peter: Five? That's going to be cutting it close. The conference I'm attending ends at 4:30. What if I get here at 6 on Sunday? Sam: It'll be another $65. Peter: There's no grace period? Sam: There's a 29 minute grace period. So, you could return the car at 5:29 and still be okay. Peter: Okay, thanks. You've been such a big help. Sam: You're very welcome. Here's the key. The car is in space A4. You're good to go.

idioms.meaning_en: to be thinking about as a possibility
idioms.meaning_vi: đang suy nghĩ về cái gì đó
idioms.example: What kind of color do you have in mind for the bedroom?
idioms.context: What size do you have in mind?
idioms.fill_sentence: I am looking for a quiet place to host our team meeting next Friday. I __________ a small coffee shop downtown, but I am open to your suggestions if you know somewhere better.

idioms.meaning_en: offer a lower price or a special deal for a limited time
idioms.meaning_vi: có chương trình khuyến mãi đặc biệt
idioms.example: The grocery store is running a special on strawberries this week.
idioms.context: We're running a special right now.
idioms.fill_sentence: Our favorite local bookstore is struggling to clear out their older stock before the summer season begins. To attract more customers, the manager decided to run a special on all hardback novels for the next three days only. We should head over there soon to take advantage of these discounted prices before the promotion expires.

idioms.meaning_en: including; already included in the amount
idioms.example: The price of the hotel room is inclusive of breakfast.
idioms.context: It's $55 a day inclusive of tax, plus insurance.
idioms.fill_sentence: We booked a full-board resort package for our upcoming summer vacation in Da Nang. The final price we paid online was inclusive of all taxes, service fees, and three meals a day, so we do not have to worry about any extra costs once we arrive.

idioms.meaning_en: to read something carefully, to review; to take a look at, often with the goal of making edits or making sure everything is okay
idioms.meaning_vi: đọc kỹ lại, xem xét lại
idioms.example: You should read the contract over before you sign it.
idioms.context: Here you go, read that over, please.
idioms.fill_sentence: I finished writing my essay for the English class, but I am worried about minor spelling errors. Before I submit the assignment to the teacher, I need to read over the document one last time to ensure everything is perfect.

idioms.idiom: not be able to make heads or tails of
idioms.meaning_en: Unable to understand or make sense of something at all, often due to extreme confusion or lack of clarity
idioms.meaning_vi: không thể hiểu rõ/không thể giải thích được
idioms.example: I can't make heads or tails of these assembly instructions.
idioms.context: I can't make heads or tails of this information.
idioms.fill_sentence: I stared at the medical report for over an hour, but the complex jargon and messy handwriting were completely confusing. Even after reading the document several times, I was simply not be able to make heads or tails of the doctor's diagnosis. It felt like I was trying to decipher an ancient, coded language.

idioms.meaning_vi: đã chuẩn bị xong/sẵn sàng/xong xuôi
idioms.example: We are all set for our trip to Japan.
idioms.fill_sentence: I have finished packing my suitcase, double-checked my flight tickets, and confirmed the hotel reservation for our upcoming trip. Now that everything is packed and organized, I am all set to leave for the airport early tomorrow morning.

idioms.meaning_en: to damage, injure or smash something (often a vehicle)
idioms.meaning_vi: làm hư hỏng, va quẹt (thường là xe cộ)
idioms.example: He banged up his car when he hit a pole in the parking lot.
idioms.context: That way, if you bang up the car, you won't owe us anything.
idioms.fill_sentence: I was devastated when I saw my brand-new car after the heavy hailstorm yesterday. The golf-ball-sized ice completely managed to bang up the hood and the roof of the vehicle. Now, I have to take it to the repair shop to fix all the dents.

idioms.meaning_en: to be prepared for a possible future event
idioms.example: Take an umbrella just in case it rains.
idioms.context: I'm sure I won't have an accident, but I'll take it just in case.
idioms.fill_sentence: I checked the weather report this morning and it predicted a high chance of heavy rain later today. Even though the sky looks clear right now, I decided to pack my umbrella just in case.

idioms.meaning_en: an extremely high price for something
idioms.meaning_vi: giá quá đắt/đắt cắt cổ (như là ăn cướp)
idioms.example: Charging $10 for a bottle of water is highway robbery.
idioms.fill_sentence: I wanted to buy a bottle of water at the airport, but they charged me ten dollars for it. That is absolute highway robbery considering how cheap it is everywhere else. I refused to pay such an outrageous price and walked away.

idioms.meaning_en: to do something with almost no margin for error, particularly regarding time or space
idioms.example: Arriving at the airport just 30 minutes before the flight means you are cutting it close.
idioms.context: That's going to be cutting it close.
idioms.fill_sentence: I woke up thirty minutes after my alarm and realized my train was scheduled to depart in less than an hour. I only arrived at the platform a few seconds before the doors locked, so I definitely cut it close today. Next time, I really need to set multiple alarms to ensure I am not rushing.

idioms.meaning_en: extra time allowed to do something without penalty
idioms.example: There is a 10-day grace period for paying your rent.
idioms.fill_sentence: I missed the deadline for my electricity bill payment by two days, but the company did not charge me a late fee. Fortunately, they offer a three-day grace period for all customers to settle their accounts without any financial penalty. This extra time saved me from paying an unnecessary extra charge.

idioms.meaning_en: ready to leave or start something
idioms.meaning_vi: sẵn sàng để bắt đầu hoặc đi
idioms.example: Once you sign these papers, you're good to go.
idioms.fill_sentence: I have finished packing my suitcase and checked that I have my passport and boarding pass. Everything is finally organized and I am good to go for my flight to London tomorrow morning.
